name: Word Counter
shortDescription: Count words, characters, sentences and estimated reading time in essays, articles and social posts.
intro: Paste an essay, draft, or social caption to measure its length before you publish. The counter reports words, Unicode characters, characters without whitespace, sentence segments, and reading time. Use the same text to compare a short edit with your original draft. Nothing leaves this browser, so you can work on a private first draft without creating an account. You can reset the workspace between separate tasks.
how: Words are groups of Unicode letters or numbers, with internal apostrophes and hyphens kept together. Reading time rounds up at 200 words per minute. Sentence segments are separated by terminal punctuation.
limitations: Character counts use Unicode code points, not visual grapheme clusters. Emoji sequences may count as multiple characters. Sentence counts are estimates; abbreviations may create extra segments. Maximum input: 100,000 characters.

faq.question: Does a hyphenated word count as one?
faq.answer: Yes. Well-written and contractions count as single words.

faq.question: How is reading time calculated?
faq.answer: The word count is divided by 200 and rounded up to whole minutes.

faq.question: Can I count non-English text?
faq.answer: Unicode letters are recognized. Languages without spaces may need a language-specific tokenizer.

name: JSON Formatter
shortDescription: Format, validate or minify JSON online with readable indentation and syntax error locations.
intro: Turn compact JSON into an indented document you can read and copy. Choose Format for two-space indentation or Minify to remove unnecessary whitespace. The validator identifies the approximate line and column of a syntax error so you can repair a missing quote, comma, or bracket. Input is parsed as data in your browser and never executed as code or uploaded to a server.
how: The browser JSON parser validates the input. The parsed value is serialized with two-space indentation, or no indentation in Minify mode.
limitations: Maximum input: 100,000 characters. JavaScript number precision applies; very large integers can lose precision. Duplicate keys retain the last value. Comments and trailing commas are not JSON. Errors identify a location, not a semantic object path.

faq.question: Can I format JSON with comments?
faq.answer: No. Remove comments and trailing commas before formatting.

faq.question: Does this reorder keys?
faq.answer: Object key ordering follows JavaScript serialization rules, including numeric keys.

faq.question: Is pasted JSON executed?
faq.answer: No. JSON is parsed as data and displayed as escaped text.

name: Percentage Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate a percentage of a number, percentage increase or decrease, and one number as a percentage of another.
intro: Find a percentage of a number, express one number as a percentage of another, or measure a percentage change. Choose the mode that matches your question, then enter the two values. This is useful for discounts, progress reports, scores, and comparisons. Results use ordinary arithmetic and remain in your browser. The labels explain the role of each number so you can check your calculation before using it.
how: Percentage of: A × B / 100. A as a percentage of B: A / B × 100. Change from A to B: (B − A) / |A| × 100.
limitations: A zero denominator has no defined percentage. Negative starting values use an absolute denominator for change. Results are displayed to two decimal places.

faq.question: Can I use decimal percentages?
faq.answer: Yes, values such as 12.5 are supported.

faq.question: Why is changing from zero rejected?
faq.answer: Percentage change divides by the starting value, and division by zero is undefined.

faq.question: Is a percentage-point change the same?
faq.answer: No. Moving from 20% to 30% is 10 percentage points and a 50% relative increase.

name: Age Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate age in years, months and days from a date of birth, with total days and the next birthday.
intro: Calculate elapsed calendar years, months, and days between a birth date and a comparison date. The comparison defaults to today on your device, but you can choose another date to check an anniversary or a form requirement. The result also reports days until the next birthday. Dates are handled as calendar values, so daylight-saving changes do not add or remove an hour from the calculation.
how: Whole years and months are counted using calendar anniversaries. When a day does not exist in a destination month it is clamped to that month’s last day. Remaining days use UTC date differences.
limitations: Birth dates must be from 1900 onward. February 29 birthdays use February 28 in non-leap years. This convention may differ from legal age rules in your location.

faq.question: Can I compare against a future date?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter that date in the comparison field.

faq.question: How are leap-day birthdays handled?
faq.answer: February 28 is used in years without February 29.

faq.question: Does time of birth matter?
faq.answer: No. This tool compares whole calendar dates, not timestamps.

name: Base64 Encoder / Decoder
shortDescription: Encode UTF-8 text to Base64 or decode Base64 back to readable text in your browser.
intro: Convert ordinary text into standard Base64, or decode Base64 back into readable UTF-8 text. Switch modes before running the transformation. This is useful when inspecting a text payload or preparing a value for a system that expects Base64. Unicode text is encoded as UTF-8 bytes first. Processing happens locally and the output can be copied directly without sending its contents to an external service.
how: Encoding converts UTF-8 bytes to the standard Base64 alphabet. Decoding validates padded Base64 and then decodes bytes as UTF-8.
limitations: Text only; arbitrary binary files are not supported. Use standard padded Base64, not Base64URL. Maximum input: 100,000 characters. Base64 is encoding, not encryption.

faq.question: Is Base64 private encryption?
faq.answer: No. Anyone with the string can decode it.

faq.question: Are emoji supported?
faq.answer: Yes, through UTF-8 encoding.

faq.question: Why did decoding fail?
faq.answer: The input may be unpadded, use the URL-safe alphabet, or contain bytes that are not valid UTF-8.

name: URL Encoder / Decoder
shortDescription: Encode URL components and query values, or decode percent-encoded text into readable characters.
intro: Encode a query value or inspect percent-encoded text without navigating to the address. Component mode escapes URL separators and is useful for a single parameter value. Full URL mode preserves the separators in a complete address. Select encode or decode, choose the scope, and run the conversion. The tool only transforms text in your browser; it does not request the pasted URL or inspect its destination.
how: Component mode uses encodeURIComponent and decodeURIComponent. Full URL mode uses encodeURI and decodeURI, preserving reserved URL delimiters.
limitations: Maximum input: 100,000 characters. A plus sign is not automatically interpreted as a space. Malformed percent escapes and invalid Unicode are rejected.

faq.question: Which mode should I choose for a query value?
faq.answer: Use Component so characters such as & and = are escaped.

faq.question: Does this open the URL?
faq.answer: No, it only transforms your text.

faq.question: Why does Full URL preserve some escapes?
faq.answer: Reserved separators are preserved to avoid changing the structure of an address.

name: UUID Generator
shortDescription: Generate random version 4 UUIDs individually or in batches, ready to copy into your project.
intro: Create one or a batch of version 4 UUIDs for development, fixtures, and identifiers. Choose a quantity between one and one hundred, then generate a fresh batch. Each identifier uses the browser’s cryptographically secure random UUID API. Results are listed one per line for copying into a file or a development tool. There is no account, remote request, or shared history of the identifiers you generate.
how: The browser crypto.randomUUID API produces random version 4 UUIDs with standard version and variant bits.

examples.output: One UUID in the pattern xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
Three independently generated UUIDs, one per line

limitations: Requires a secure context such as HTTPS or localhost. Random identifiers have extremely low but nonzero collision probability. UUIDs are not passwords or access tokens.

faq.question: Are these version 4 UUIDs?
faq.answer: Yes, they are cryptographically random v4 UUIDs.

faq.question: Can I generate the same UUID again?
faq.answer: There is no seed or deterministic mode.

faq.question: How many can I generate at once?
faq.answer: Between 1 and 100. Use another run for a fresh batch.

name: Slug Generator
shortDescription: Create a clean URL slug from a title with hyphens, underscores or supported Unicode letters.
intro: Turn a heading or article title into a consistent URL segment. Choose a hyphen or underscore separator, then decide whether to keep Unicode letters. The default ASCII mode removes accents where normalization permits it and drops unsupported characters. The result is lowercase with repeated punctuation replaced by a single separator. This is a text transformation only; check your own website for duplicate slugs before publishing a page.
how: NFKD normalization separates compatible forms and accents. Combining marks are removed, letters are lowercased, and runs of unsupported characters become the selected separator.
limitations: Maximum input: 100,000 characters. ASCII mode is not transliteration: scripts without Latin equivalents may disappear. Unicode mode retains letters and digits but removes combining marks.

faq.question: Should I use hyphens or underscores?
faq.answer: Hyphens are the default. Match your existing site’s URL convention.

faq.question: Will Chinese letters be retained?
faq.answer: Yes, when Keep Unicode letters is selected.

faq.question: Does this ensure the URL is unique?
faq.answer: No. Check for an existing page with the same slug in your site.

name: UTM Link Builder
shortDescription: Build campaign tracking URLs with UTM source, medium, campaign, term and content parameters.
intro: Add campaign tags to an HTTP or HTTPS address without manually escaping each value. Enter the destination, source, medium, and campaign name; term and content are optional. The builder keeps unrelated query parameters and the fragment while replacing existing standard UTM fields. Copy the finished address into your campaign workflow. No address is opened or submitted, and the builder does not connect to an analytics provider.
how: The URL API validates the address and URLSearchParams serializes five standard UTM parameters. Blank optional fields remove their existing values.
limitations: Destination limit: 8,192 characters; each campaign field: 200 characters. Only HTTP and HTTPS without embedded credentials are accepted. Avoid personal information in tags.

faq.question: Are existing query parameters kept?
faq.answer: Yes, unrelated parameters and the URL fragment are preserved.

faq.question: Are tags case sensitive?
faq.answer: Analytics tools can distinguish different capitalization. Choose a consistent convention.

faq.question: Does this measure clicks?
faq.answer: No. Your destination’s analytics system interprets the tags.

name: SIP Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate SIP returns, total investment and projected value with a growth chart and monthly or yearly investment breakdown.
intro: Estimate a future balance from a fixed monthly contribution and an assumed annual return. Adjust the amount, number of years, rate, and whether deposits occur at the beginning or end of each month. The result separates contributions from estimated growth, helping you understand the effect of time and assumptions. This is a simplified mathematical illustration. It does not predict any investment’s performance or recommend a product.
how: Monthly rate r = annual rate / 12 / 100; n = years × 12. End-month value = P × ((1+r)^n − 1) / r. Beginning-month deposits multiply that result by (1+r). A zero rate returns contributions only.
limitations: Assumes constant returns with monthly compounding and regular deposits. Excludes taxes, fees, inflation, and market volatility. Returns are not guaranteed. Amounts use your selected currency as a display unit.

faq.question: Does the rate mean a guaranteed return?
faq.answer: No. It is only an assumption for the projection.

faq.question: When are contributions made?
faq.answer: Choose beginning or end of month. Beginning-month deposits grow for one additional month.

faq.question: Does this account for inflation?
faq.answer: No. Results are nominal and do not account for changes in purchasing power.

name: Nutrition Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate daily calorie needs and protein, fat and carbohydrate grams using your measurements and activity level.
intro: Estimate adult daily energy needs from height, weight, age, the selected formula sex coefficient, and an activity multiplier. Set protein and fat percentages to see an illustrative split in grams, with carbohydrates taking the remainder. This general tool is for adults aged 18 and over and is not a meal plan. It is not suitable for pregnancy, breastfeeding, eating disorders, medical conditions, or decisions about medication or supplements.
how: The simplified Mifflin–St Jeor equation is 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age, plus 5 for the male coefficient or minus 161 for the female coefficient. Resting energy is multiplied by the chosen activity factor. Protein and carbohydrate use 4 kcal/g; fat uses 9 kcal/g.

examples.input: Male coefficient, 70 kg, 175 cm, 30 years, factor 1.2

examples.output: 100 g protein; 66.67 g fat; 250 g carbohydrate

limitations: General estimates only, not diagnosis, treatment, or an individualized diet. Activity multipliers are rough assumptions. Consult a qualified healthcare professional for decisions affecting health. Formula content awaits human review before indexing.

faq.question: Is this a weight-loss plan?
faq.answer: No. The output estimates maintenance energy under the assumptions you choose.

faq.question: Why does the formula ask for sex?
faq.answer: The original equation has two sex coefficients. This is a model limitation, not a complete description of individual physiology.

faq.question: Can children or pregnant people use it?
faq.answer: No. Their needs require a different assessment with an appropriate professional.

name: BMI Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate adult body mass index from height and weight in metric or imperial units, with category context.
intro: Calculate body mass index using height and weight, then see the corresponding adult screening category. Metric and imperial inputs are supported and converted before calculation. This tool uses CDC adult categories for people aged 20 and over. BMI is a broad screening measure and does not directly measure body fat or individual health. Consider the result alongside other information and professional advice when making decisions about your health.
how: BMI = weight in kilograms / (height in meters)². Categories use the unrounded result: below 18.5, underweight; 18.5 to below 25, healthy weight; 25 to below 30, overweight; 30 and above, obesity.
limitations: Only for adults aged 20 or older. Not a diagnostic test, body-fat measurement, or pregnancy assessment. Muscularity and other individual factors can affect interpretation. Consult a qualified healthcare professional. Content awaits human review before indexing.

faq.question: Why is the minimum age 20?
faq.answer: CDC adult categories apply to ages 20 and over. Children and teens use age- and sex-specific percentiles.

faq.question: Does BMI measure body fat?
faq.answer: No. It is a ratio of weight to squared height.

faq.question: Can I use pounds and inches?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Imperial and the inputs are converted to kilograms and centimeters.

name: Image Compressor
shortDescription: Compress JPG, PNG and WebP images in your browser. Preview image quality and compare output file size before downloading.
intro: Reduce an image’s file size before sharing it, attaching it to an email, or adding it to a website. Choose a JPG, PNG, or WebP, set a quality level, and compare the original size with the new file. You can also set maximum dimensions and choose an output format. The preview and downloaded result are generated on your device, so no file is uploaded to a service.
how: The image is decoded into pixels in a browser worker, fitted within the maximum dimensions without upscaling, and re-encoded as WebP, JPG, or PNG. Quality affects lossy JPG and WebP. PNG uses lossless encoding.

examples.output: 1,080 × 540 output; exact file size depends on the image

limitations: One JPG, PNG, or WebP up to 20 MB and 12 million pixels. Output sides are limited to 4,096 pixels. Compression savings vary and a result can be larger. PNG ignores quality. JPG replaces transparency with white. Animation, EXIF, and color profiles are not preserved. Web Workers and OffscreenCanvas are required.

faq.question: Does my photo get uploaded?
faq.answer: No. A browser worker processes it on your device.

faq.question: Why is the result larger?
faq.answer: Some source files are already well optimized. Try WebP, lower quality, or smaller dimensions.

faq.question: Is quality 80 lossless?
faq.answer: No. JPG and WebP at that setting are lossy. PNG retains the rendered pixels but may increase file size.

name: Image Resizer
shortDescription: Resize an image to fit a chosen width and height in pixels while preserving its aspect ratio, then preview and download.
intro: Fit an image into the dimensions you need for a website, email, or creative project. Enter a maximum width and height, or start with a Web, Social, or Email preset. The image keeps its original proportions and is never stretched or enlarged. You can check the output dimensions and preview before downloading. Processing takes place locally in a browser worker rather than uploading your image to a remote service.
how: The scale is the smaller of maximum width / original width, maximum height / original height, and 1. Both dimensions are multiplied by that scale and rounded to whole pixels. The output fits inside the requested box.
limitations: This is fit-within resizing, not cropping or an exact social-platform template. One image up to 20 MB and 12 million pixels. Maximum output side 4,096 pixels. Re-encoding can remove metadata and animation. JPG flattens transparency to white.

faq.question: Will it crop my photo?
faq.answer: No. The entire image fits within the chosen box.

faq.question: Can I make a small photo bigger?
faq.answer: This tool does not upscale. Small inputs keep their original dimensions.

faq.question: What do the presets mean?
faq.answer: They are convenient maximum-size boxes, not guarantees of current platform upload requirements.

name: Merge PDF
shortDescription: Merge multiple PDF files into one document. Arrange the file order and download the combined PDF locally.
intro: Combine separate PDFs into a single document for sharing, applications, or project handoffs. Choose your files, then use the up and down controls to put them in the right order. Every page from the first file is followed by the pages from the next file. Your documents are processed inside a browser worker and the final PDF is downloaded directly, with no account or upload required.
how: A new PDF is created and pages are copied from each source document in the displayed file order. The page-count limit is checked before pages are added. Processing can be canceled or times out after 45 seconds.

examples.input: A 2-page PDF followed by a 3-page PDF
Move file B above file A
examples.output: Pages from B appear before pages from A

limitations: Two to ten files, up to 20 MB each, 30 MB combined, and 200 total pages. Password-protected or damaged PDFs are not supported. Bookmarks, signatures, forms, attachments, and document-level features may not survive. This is not a PDF security sanitizer. Review the downloaded result before sharing.

faq.question: Can I change the order?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the up and down buttons before merging.

faq.question: Does merging shrink the files?
faq.answer: No. This tool combines pages; it does not optimize PDF size.

faq.question: Are signed PDFs still signed afterward?
faq.answer: No. Creating a new document does not preserve the validity of source digital signatures.

name: Images to PDF
shortDescription: Convert JPG, PNG and WebP images into a PDF document with control over page order and layout.
intro: Create a PDF from photos, scans, or design exports without installing a document editor. Add JPG, PNG, or WebP images and arrange the files in the order you want. Each image is centered on its own A4 page with margins and its proportions preserved. This is useful for collecting receipts or sharing a visual reference pack. The images stay in your browser while the PDF is assembled.
how: Each image is fitted within 2,400 × 2,400 pixels, flattened on white, and encoded as a high-quality JPEG. It is then centered inside the margins of a portrait A4 PDF page. There is one page per image, in the selected order.

examples.output: One PDF with three A4 pages
Centered on a portrait A4 page without cropping

limitations: Up to ten images, 20 MB each and 30 MB combined. Each image must be no more than 12 million pixels. Images are re-encoded with lossy JPEG and white backgrounds. Text remains an image, not selectable or searchable text. This tool does not perform OCR.

faq.question: Can I select text in the PDF?
faq.answer: No. The PDF contains images; no optical character recognition is performed.

faq.question: Are transparent backgrounds preserved?
faq.answer: No. Transparent areas are flattened to white before PDF creation.

faq.question: Can I rearrange the pages?
faq.answer: Yes. Reorder your input images before creating the PDF.

name: QR Code Generator
shortDescription: Create a static QR code for a URL or text, customize its appearance and download it for print or sharing.
intro: Make a static QR code for a website address or short piece of text. Paste the content, choose a dark ink color and PNG size, then create and download the result. Print it on a card or use it in a digital design after testing it with the intended scanner. The code contains exactly your entered content, without a tracking redirect, account, or expiry controlled by ToolzPoint.
how: Content is encoded as a standard QR symbol with medium error correction and a four-module white quiet zone. Dark color options preserve strong contrast against white. PNG exports are available at 320, 640, and 1,280 pixels.

examples.output: A QR code that decodes to exactly https://example.com
A QR code containing the text Hello, world!

limitations: Maximum 1,000 UTF-8 bytes. Dense codes require adequate printed size and a good scanner. The PNG does not expire, but a linked website can change or disappear. Test the downloaded code before printing. Changing a destination requires generating and replacing the static QR code.

faq.question: Does the QR code expire?
faq.answer: The static code itself does not expire. Availability of its linked destination is separate.

faq.question: Can I edit the link after printing?
faq.answer: No. The link is stored in the symbol itself. Generate and replace the code if it changes.

faq.question: Does it track scans?
faq.answer: No. ToolzPoint adds no tracking redirect or scan analytics.

name: Password Generator
shortDescription: Generate random passwords with configurable length, letters, numbers and symbols using browser cryptographic randomness.
intro: Generate one or several random passwords of a length and character mix you choose. Pick any combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols, then set how many characters and how many passwords you want at once. Every character is chosen using your browser's cryptographic random number generator, the same source used for security-sensitive code, rather than an ordinary pseudo-random function. Nothing you generate here is transmitted anywhere or stored; if you close the tab without copying a password, it is gone for good, so copy it into your password manager right away.
how: Each character is picked uniformly from the character sets you enable, using the Web Crypto API's getRandomValues with rejection sampling to avoid bias toward any character. Length ranges from 6 to 128, and you can generate up to 20 passwords in one run.

examples.output: A random 16-character password such as aK9pXq2mZt7RbN4c
Three independent 24-character passwords, one per line

limitations: At least one character type must be selected. Very short lengths combined with every character type enabled do not guarantee every type appears in a single password, since each character is chosen independently. This tool cannot check whether a site accepts the symbols it generates.

faq.question: Is this as secure as a password manager's generator?
faq.answer: The randomness source is the same browser API most password managers use. Unlike a manager, ToolzPoint does not store or sync the result, so save it yourself right away.

faq.question: Why avoid similar-looking characters?
faq.answer: This generator does not filter look-alike characters like 1, l, and I. If a site requires manual re-entry, double-check ambiguous characters before saving.

faq.question: How long should my password be?
faq.answer: Longer is stronger. Twelve characters with mixed types is a reasonable minimum; sixteen or more is better where the site allows it.

name: Coin Flip
shortDescription: Flip a virtual coin once or in batches. See heads and tails counts and the sequence of random results.
intro: Flip a virtual coin when you need a quick, unbiased decision, or flip many at once to see how heads and tails balance out over a larger sample. Enter how many times to flip, from a single toss up to a thousand, and the tool reports how many landed heads, how many landed tails, and the order they fell in for smaller runs. Each flip uses an independent fifty-fifty random draw in your browser, so results are not influenced by previous flips or by anything on this page.
how: Each flip draws a random number and treats it as heads below 0.5 and tails otherwise. Requesting twenty flips or fewer also lists the full sequence in order; larger runs report only the totals to keep the result readable.

examples.output: Heads: about 50 · Tails: about 50 (exact split varies by run)

limitations: Maximum 1,000 flips per run. Results are pseudo-random, suitable for casual decisions and demonstrations, not for cryptography or regulated gambling. The sequence list is only shown for 20 flips or fewer.

faq.question: Is the coin actually fair?
faq.answer: Each flip has an independent 50% chance of either outcome, the same as an ideal fair coin, using your browser's random number generator.

faq.question: Can I flip more than one coin at a time?
faq.answer: Yes. Set any number from 1 to 1,000 to flip that many coins and see the combined heads and tails count.

faq.question: Why don't I see every result for 500 flips?
faq.answer: The full sequence is only listed for 20 flips or fewer so the result stays readable. Larger runs show totals instead.

name: EMI / Loan Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate monthly EMI, total loan interest and repayment cost with a monthly or yearly amortization schedule.
intro: Estimate the equal monthly installment on a home, car, or personal loan from the amount borrowed, the annual interest rate, and the repayment period in years. The result breaks the loan down into the monthly payment, the total interest paid over its full term, and the total amount repaid altogether. This uses the standard reducing-balance EMI formula that most lenders use for fixed-rate loans, so you can sanity-check a lender's quote or compare two different rates or terms before committing to either one.
how: Monthly EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100), and n is the number of monthly installments. A zero interest rate simplifies to the loan amount divided evenly by the number of months.
limitations: Assumes a fixed interest rate for the full term with no prepayments, fees, or insurance added. Real loans may compound or apply charges differently; treat this as an estimate to compare scenarios, not a binding repayment schedule from a lender.

faq.question: What does EMI stand for?
faq.answer: Equal Monthly Installment: the fixed payment you make each month that covers both interest and principal over the loan term.

faq.question: Does this include processing fees or insurance?
faq.answer: No. It calculates the pure interest-and-principal payment. Add any fees your lender charges separately when budgeting.

faq.question: How does a shorter term change the EMI?
faq.answer: A shorter term raises the monthly EMI but lowers the total interest paid, since less time is spent accruing interest on the remaining balance.

name: Compound Interest Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate compound interest and maturity value with a growth chart, monthly and yearly schedules, and CSV export.
intro: Project how a lump sum grows over time when interest compounds at a chosen frequency instead of being paid out as simple interest. Enter the principal, the annual interest rate, the number of years, and how often interest compounds, from annually down to daily, to see the final maturity amount and the interest earned on top of what you put in. Compounding more frequently at the same stated rate produces a slightly larger result, because each period's interest starts earning its own interest sooner.
how: Maturity amount = P × (1 + r ÷ n)^(n × t), where P is the principal, r is the annual rate as a decimal, n is the number of compounding periods per year, and t is the time in years. Interest earned is the maturity amount minus the principal.
limitations: Assumes a fixed rate and no additional deposits or withdrawals during the period. Real accounts may compound on slightly different schedules or apply fees and taxes that reduce the effective return.

faq.question: Why does compounding frequency matter?
faq.answer: More frequent compounding lets interest start earning its own interest sooner, so daily compounding yields marginally more than annual compounding at the same stated rate.

faq.question: How is this different from the SIP calculator?
faq.answer: This tool projects a single lump-sum deposit. The SIP calculator instead projects regular monthly contributions added over time.

faq.question: Can I use this for a savings account?
faq.answer: Yes, as a general estimate. Confirm your bank's actual compounding frequency and any fees, which can differ from the assumptions here.

name: Temperature Converter
shortDescription: Switch between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin.
intro: Convert a temperature between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin by entering a value and choosing the units to convert from and to. This covers everyday conversions like checking a weather forecast reported in an unfamiliar scale, following a recipe from another country, or converting a scientific reading to Kelvin. The tool validates that a Kelvin or converted value never falls below absolute zero, the coldest physically possible temperature, and reports a clear error if the input would require it.
how: Every conversion passes through Celsius as an intermediate step: Fahrenheit to Celsius is (F − 32) × 5⁄9, and Celsius to Kelvin adds 273.15. The reverse formulas convert back out to the requested unit.
limitations: Rejects any value that would fall below absolute zero (−273.15 °C, −459.67 °F, or 0 K). Results are shown to two decimal places, which may round very precise scientific values.

faq.question: What is absolute zero?
faq.answer: Absolute zero is 0 Kelvin, −273.15 °C, or −459.67 °F: the coldest temperature theoretically possible, where this tool stops accepting a colder input.

faq.question: Can I convert Fahrenheit directly to Kelvin?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Fahrenheit as the source and Kelvin as the target; the tool converts through Celsius internally and returns the Kelvin value.

faq.question: Why does my result have decimals?
faq.answer: Fahrenheit and Celsius conversions rarely land on whole numbers because of the 5⁄9 scaling factor. Results are rounded to two decimal places for readability.

name: Discount Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate the sale price after a percentage discount and see exactly how much you save.
intro: Work out the final price of an item after a percentage discount, along with exactly how much money the discount saves. Enter the original price and the discount percentage to see both figures at once, which is useful for comparing sale offers, checking a cashier's math, or planning a budget around seasonal discounts. The calculation is ordinary arithmetic performed entirely in your browser, so you can check several offers in a row without any of the amounts leaving your device.
how: The amount saved is the original price multiplied by the discount percentage divided by 100. The sale price is the original price minus that saved amount.
limitations: Accepts a discount between 0% and 100%. Does not account for taxes, additional fees, or stacked discounts applied one after another, which can produce a different final price than a single combined percentage.

faq.question: Does this handle two discounts applied one after another?
faq.answer: No. Enter the first discount, note the sale price, then run the calculator again on that new price for a second discount, since stacked percentages do not simply add together.

faq.question: Can the discount be more than 100%?
faq.answer: No. A discount above 100% would mean a negative price, so the tool caps the input at 100%.

faq.question: Does this include sales tax?
faq.answer: No. It calculates the discount on the original price only. Add tax separately based on your local rate and whether it applies before or after the discount.

name: Ideal Weight Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate a general reference body weight using the Devine formula, with results in kilograms and pounds.
intro: Estimate a general reference body weight from height using the Devine formula, a method originally published in 1974 and still widely cited for drug-dosing and clinical reference calculations. Enter a height and select male or female, since the formula uses a different starting point for each, and see the estimated ideal weight in both kilograms and pounds. This is a population-level reference point, not a personal target: healthy weight depends on frame size, muscle mass, age, and many other factors this simple formula does not consider.
how: Devine formula: for men, 50 kg plus 2.3 kg for each inch of height over 5 feet; for women, 45.5 kg plus 2.3 kg for each inch over 5 feet. Height is converted from centimeters to inches above the 5-foot mark before applying the multiplier.
limitations: Valid for heights between 140 cm and 230 cm. The Devine formula was designed as a clinical dosing reference, not a fitness or beauty target, and does not account for muscle mass, bone density, or body frame. It is not medical advice.

faq.question: Is this the same as a healthy BMI range?
faq.answer: No. This uses the height-based Devine formula, while the BMI calculator uses weight divided by height squared. The two methods can give different reference numbers.

faq.question: Why does the formula differ by sex?
faq.answer: The Devine formula uses separate baseline constants for men and women, reflecting average differences in body composition observed in the original clinical population it was derived from.

faq.question: Should I use this number as a personal goal?
faq.answer: Treat it as a general reference point only. A qualified healthcare professional can account for your frame, muscle mass, and health history far better than a single formula.

name: Case Converter
shortDescription: Switch text between UPPER, lower, Title, and more.
intro: Paste any text and convert it to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, snake_case, or kebab-case in one click. This is useful for tidying up headlines, preparing variable names while coding, or fixing text that was typed with the caps lock key stuck on. Word boundaries for camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case are detected from spaces and punctuation, so a normal sentence converts cleanly into a single compact identifier. Everything runs in your browser, so drafts stay private until you choose to copy them elsewhere.
how: UPPERCASE and lowercase apply directly. Title Case capitalizes the first letter of each word. Sentence case capitalizes the first letter of the text and after each sentence-ending punctuation mark. camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case split the text into words at non-letter, non-number boundaries and rejoin them with the chosen style.

examples.input: "hello world. this is great!" → Sentence case

limitations: Maximum input: 100,000 characters. Sentence case relies on periods, question marks, and exclamation points to find sentence boundaries, so abbreviations such as “Dr.” may create an unwanted capital letter afterward. camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case discard punctuation from the original text.

faq.question: Will this preserve my line breaks?
faq.answer: UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, and Sentence case preserve line breaks and spacing. camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case join everything into a single continuous identifier.

faq.question: How are contractions like "don't" handled in Title Case?
faq.answer: The apostrophe and the letters after it are kept with the word, so “don't stop” becomes “Don't Stop” rather than splitting at the apostrophe.

faq.question: Can I convert code identifiers back to plain words?
faq.answer: Not directly. This tool converts plain text into a case style; splitting an existing camelCase or snake_case identifier back into words is not supported.

name: Hash Generator
shortDescription: Compute SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 digests.
intro: Compute a cryptographic hash digest of any text using SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512, the algorithm families most commonly required for checksums, commit identifiers, and integrity checks. Paste or type text, choose an algorithm, and get the resulting digest as a lowercase hexadecimal string ready to compare or paste elsewhere. Hashing runs through your browser's built-in Web Crypto API, the same implementation browsers use for secure connections, so the text never leaves this page during the calculation.
how: The text is encoded as UTF-8 bytes and passed to the Web Crypto API's digest function for the selected algorithm. The resulting byte array is converted to a lowercase hexadecimal string, two characters per byte.

examples.input: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" (SHA-256)
"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" (SHA-1)

limitations: Maximum input: 100,000 characters. SHA-1 is no longer considered collision-resistant for adversarial security use, though it remains fine for checksums and non-adversarial comparisons. MD5 is not offered because it is not implemented by the browser's cryptographic API.

faq.question: Which algorithm should I use?
faq.answer: SHA-256 is the most common general-purpose choice today. Use SHA-1 only for compatibility with older systems, and SHA-384 or SHA-512 where a longer digest is required.

faq.question: Can I hash a file instead of text?
faq.answer: Not with this tool. It hashes the text you paste or type; hashing a file's binary contents needs a dedicated file-hashing tool.

faq.question: Is hashing the same as encryption?
faq.answer: No. Hashing is one-way and cannot be reversed to recover the original text. Encryption is reversible with the correct key.

name: JWT Decoder
shortDescription: Read the header and payload inside a JWT.
intro: Paste a JSON Web Token to see its header and payload decoded into readable, indented JSON, without needing a backend or command-line tool. A JWT is three Base64URL-encoded sections separated by dots: a header describing the signing algorithm, a payload carrying the claims, and a signature. This tool decodes the first two sections so you can inspect claims like expiry and subject while debugging an authentication flow, and displays the signature as-is since verifying it correctly requires the issuer's secret or public key, which this tool never asks for or receives.
how: Each of the header and payload sections is Base64URL-decoded, padded as needed, and parsed as JSON, then re-serialized with two-space indentation. The signature section is shown unmodified and is explicitly labeled as not verified.

examples.output: Error: the header is not valid Base64URL-encoded JSON

limitations: This tool decodes only; it does not verify the signature, so a decoded payload should never be treated as authenticated without separately checking the signature against the issuer's key. Maximum input: 100,000 characters.

faq.question: Does this verify that the token is genuine?
faq.answer: No. Verifying a JWT signature requires the issuer's secret or public key, which this tool never requests. It only decodes the readable header and payload.

faq.question: Why does my token fail to decode?
faq.answer: A JWT needs exactly three dot-separated parts. Check that you copied the complete token, including all three sections, without extra whitespace.

faq.question: Is my token uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No. Decoding happens entirely in your browser using standard Base64 and JSON parsing; the token is never sent to a server.

name: Meta Tag Generator
shortDescription: Build title, description, and Open Graph tags.
intro: Generate a ready-to-paste block of HTML meta tags from a page title, description, canonical URL, and optional share image and site name. The output covers the basics search engines read, plus Open Graph and Twitter Card tags that control how the page's link preview looks when shared on social platforms and messaging apps. Filling in one form instead of hand-writing a dozen tags reduces the chance of a typo breaking a preview image or leaving a description blank on a shared link.
how: Each field is validated for length and, where relevant, as a proper URL, then HTML-escaped and inserted into a title tag, a meta description, a canonical link, and the corresponding Open Graph and Twitter Card meta tags. The Twitter card type switches to a large-image layout automatically when a share image is provided.

examples.input: Title "ToolzPoint", description "Free browser tools", URL https://www.toolzpointt.com/
examples.output: <title>ToolzPoint</title> plus matching description, canonical, Open Graph, and Twitter tags

examples.input: Same fields, with a share image URL added
examples.output: Adds og:image and twitter:image, and switches twitter:card to summary_large_image

limitations: Title is capped at 70 characters and description at 200 characters to match common search-result truncation points; longer text is rejected rather than silently cut. This tool does not verify that the image URL actually resolves to an image.

faq.question: Where do these tags go on my page?
faq.answer: Paste the generated block inside your HTML document's <head> section, before the closing </head> tag.

faq.question: Is a share image required?
faq.answer: No, it's optional. Without one, links typically preview with just the title and description and no image.

faq.question: Will this guarantee my exact description shows in search results?
faq.answer: No. Search engines may rewrite the displayed snippet based on the query. The meta description is a strong hint, not a guarantee.

name: Split PDF
shortDescription: Extract selected pages or page ranges from a PDF and download them as a separate document.
intro: Choose one PDF and a list of page numbers or ranges to extract into a brand-new PDF, leaving the original file untouched. This is the reverse of combining files with Merge PDF: instead of joining documents together, it pulls out just the pages you need, such as a single chapter, a signed page, or an appendix, without opening a full desktop PDF editor. Processing happens with a PDF library running in your browser, so the file is read, split, and rebuilt entirely on your device.
how: The PDF is parsed to count its pages, then your page list, such as “1-3, 5, 8-10”, is expanded into individual page numbers and validated against that count. The matching pages are copied in ascending order into a new PDF document, which is then offered as a download.

examples.output: A new 7-page PDF containing pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, and 10
Error: page 15 does not exist in this 12-page PDF

limitations: One PDF at a time, up to 20 MB. Encrypted or password-protected PDFs are not supported. Extracted pages always come out in ascending page order, regardless of the order typed in the range list.

faq.question: How do I write a page range?
faq.answer: Separate individual pages and ranges with commas, such as “1-3, 5, 8-10”. Ranges use a hyphen between the first and last page to keep.

faq.question: Does this change the original PDF?
faq.answer: No. The original file stays on your device unchanged; a new PDF containing only the pages you chose is created for download.

faq.question: Can I split an encrypted PDF?
faq.answer: No. Remove the password using the PDF's original source application first, then split the unprotected file here.

name: Passport & ID Photo Maker
shortDescription: Crop, resize, recolor the background, and compress a photo for passports, visas, and forms.
intro: Turn an ordinary photo into a correctly sized passport, visa, PAN card, or government-exam photo. Choose a document type and this tool crops your photo to the exact required aspect ratio, resizes it to the precise pixel dimensions those documents need, and compresses it to fit any stated file-size limit. Use the zoom and vertical-position controls to frame your face the way most application forms require. An optional background step estimates your existing background color from the photo's edges and fades it to white, sky blue, light gray, red, or any custom color you pick, which suits forms that specify a particular background color.
how: Standard document sizes are stored in millimeters and converted to pixels at 300 DPI. The photo is cropped to the target aspect ratio around its center, shifted by your zoom and vertical-position settings, then drawn onto a canvas at the exact target pixel size. If background replacement is on, the average color along the image's edges is sampled and pixels close to that color are faded toward your chosen color, with a soft-edged threshold rather than a hard cutout. When a preset specifies a maximum file size, JPEG quality is reduced step by step until the output fits.

examples.input: A selfie, preset: India Passport (3.5 × 4.5 cm)
examples.output: A 413 × 531 pixel JPEG cropped to your face and shoulders

examples.input: A selfie against a light wall, background replacement on, color white
examples.output: The same crop with its background faded to solid white

limitations: Background replacement estimates a single background color from the photo's edges and is not AI subject segmentation, so it works best with a plain, evenly lit original background; a patterned, shadowed, or cluttered background can leave halos or incomplete edges around hair and shoulders. This tool cannot correct poor lighting or verify that a photo meets every rule of a specific passport or visa authority. Always confirm current requirements with the issuing authority before submitting. Maximum one photo, 20 MB.

faq.question: Can this remove any background like an AI photo editor?
faq.answer: Not quite. It estimates one background color from the photo's edges and fades matching areas to your chosen color. A plain, evenly lit original background gives the cleanest result; a busy or shadowed one may leave visible edges.

faq.question: Can I use this for a country not in the preset list?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Custom size and enter the required width and height in millimeters.

faq.question: Why would I need a colored background instead of white?
faq.answer: Some visa and ID photo rules specify a particular background color, such as light blue or red, rather than white. Pick a preset swatch or enter a custom color to match what's required.

name: Date Difference Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate days between two dates and compare the interval in calendar years, months, weeks and days.
intro: Find out exactly how much time separates two dates, in calendar years, months, and days, as well as the total number of days and weeks. This is useful for measuring a project timeline, a contract term, time served, or the gap until a deadline or anniversary, without counting on a calendar by hand. Unlike the age calculator, which always measures from a birth date to today, this tool accepts any two dates you choose, in either order of entry as long as the start is not after the end.
how: The calendar breakdown counts whole years and months using anniversary dates, then reports the remaining days, mirroring how the age calculator counts a birthday. Total days and total weeks are a straight count of days between the two calendar dates.

examples.output: 0 years, 8 months, 18 days · 261 total days · 37 total weeks
1 year, 5 months, 14 days · 531 total days · 75 total weeks

limitations: The start date must be on or before the end date. Maximum span is bounded by JavaScript's native date range, and dates before 1900 are not specifically validated for calendar accuracy.

faq.question: How is this different from the age calculator?
faq.answer: The age calculator always measures from a birth date to today or another chosen date. This tool measures between any two dates you enter, for tasks unrelated to age.

faq.question: Does it count the start and end day both?
faq.answer: Total days is the count of days between the two calendar dates, so the start date itself is day zero, matching how most deadline and duration calculations work.

faq.question: Can I get just the answer in weeks?
faq.answer: Yes, the total weeks figure is the total days divided by seven and rounded down to a whole week.

name: Pregnancy Due Date Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate a pregnancy due date and gestational age from the last menstrual period and average cycle length.
intro: Estimate a pregnancy due date from the first day of your last menstrual period, adjusted for your average cycle length, using Naegele's rule, the standard method taught in obstetric care. Enter the date and your typical cycle length to see the estimated due date, how many weeks and days into the pregnancy you are as of today or another date, and which trimester that falls in. This is a widely used population estimate; only around one in twenty births happen exactly on the calculated due date, so an ultrasound dating scan from a healthcare provider is more precise for any individual pregnancy.
how: Naegele's rule adds 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of the last menstrual period, then adjusts by the difference between your cycle length and the textbook 28-day cycle. Weeks and days pregnant are counted from that same start date to the comparison date.
limitations: Naegele's rule assumes regular cycles and is a population-level estimate, not a diagnosis. It does not account for irregular cycles, assisted conception dating, or ultrasound measurements. This tool is not a substitute for prenatal care; confirm dating with a healthcare provider.

faq.question: How accurate is this estimate?
faq.answer: It is a widely used starting estimate. Only a small share of babies arrive on the exact calculated date; a full-term birth any time from about three weeks before to two weeks after is considered normal.

faq.question: What if my cycle isn't 28 days?
faq.answer: Enter your typical average cycle length and the calculation shifts the due date to account for it, since ovulation timing shifts with cycle length.

faq.question: Which trimester does each week fall into?
faq.answer: This tool reports weeks under 13 as the first trimester, 13 through 26 as the second, and 27 onward as the third, a common convention.

name: Ovulation Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate ovulation and fertile-window dates from the first day of a period and the average cycle length.
intro: Estimate your likely ovulation day, fertile window, and next expected period from the first day of your last period and your average cycle length. This is commonly used when trying to conceive or simply to understand your own cycle better. The estimate relies on the observation that ovulation typically occurs about fourteen days before the next period starts, regardless of how long the overall cycle runs, so a longer or shorter cycle shifts the ovulation day earlier or later without changing that fourteen-day gap at the end.
how: Ovulation day is estimated as your cycle length minus fourteen days after the start of your last period. The fertile window covers the five days before ovulation through one day after, reflecting typical sperm and egg survival times. The next period is estimated one full cycle length after the last one.
limitations: This estimate assumes a consistent luteal (post-ovulation) phase of about fourteen days, which varies between individuals. It is not a contraceptive method and not a substitute for a fertility monitor, ovulation test, or medical advice.

faq.question: Is this a reliable form of birth control?
faq.answer: No. This is a general estimate, not a validated contraceptive method. Speak with a healthcare provider about reliable contraception options.

faq.question: Why does a longer cycle push ovulation later?
faq.answer: The days after ovulation are relatively constant at about fourteen, so a longer cycle means more days occur before ovulation, pushing the estimated day later.

faq.question: How wide is the fertile window?
faq.answer: This tool estimates a six-day window: five days before ovulation, when sperm can survive to meet an egg, through one day after ovulation.

name: GST Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate GST-inclusive or GST-exclusive prices with base amount, total tax and CGST/SGST split.
intro: Calculate Goods and Services Tax the way Indian invoices need it, either by adding GST on top of a base price or by extracting how much of a GST-inclusive total is tax. Choose your direction, enter the amount and the applicable rate, such as the common 5%, 12%, 18%, or 28% slabs, and see the base price, GST amount, an even CGST and SGST split, and the total. This suits shopkeepers, freelancers, and shoppers who want to check an invoice or quote without doing the arithmetic by hand.
how: Adding GST: GST amount equals the base price multiplied by the rate divided by 100, and the total is the base price plus that GST amount. Extracting GST: the base price equals the total divided by one plus the rate divided by 100, and the GST amount is the total minus that base price. For an intra-state sale, CGST and SGST each take half of the GST amount.
limitations: This calculates standard single-rate GST only; it does not handle mixed-rate invoices, GST composition scheme rules, reverse charge, or exemptions. Confirm the applicable rate and scheme for your specific goods or services.

faq.question: What's the difference between CGST and SGST?
faq.answer: For a sale within the same state, GST splits evenly into Central GST and State GST. For an inter-state sale, the full amount is instead charged as Integrated GST (IGST), which this tool reports as the combined GST amount.

faq.question: Which mode should I use for a shop receipt?
faq.answer: If the listed price already includes tax, use "Extract GST from a total price." If you're building a quote from a pre-tax price, use "Add GST to a base price."

faq.question: Can I use a custom GST rate?
faq.answer: Yes, enter any percentage; the common slabs of 5, 12, 18, and 28 are just typical starting points.

name: Water Intake Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate a general daily water intake from body weight and activity level, with clear limits to the estimate.
intro: Get a general daily water intake target based on your body weight and activity level. Enter your weight and choose sedentary, moderate, or active, and see a suggested daily total in liters and in 250 milliliter glasses. This uses a commonly cited baseline of about 35 milliliters per kilogram of body weight, scaled up slightly for more active days, as a simple starting point rather than a precise medical prescription, since actual needs vary with climate, health conditions, and diet.
how: Baseline intake is 35 mL multiplied by your body weight in kilograms. That baseline is then scaled by 1.0 for sedentary, 1.1 for moderate, or 1.2 for active, and converted to liters and to a count of 250 mL glasses.
limitations: This is a general estimate, not medical advice. It does not account for climate, pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, or medical conditions that change fluid needs. People with kidney, heart, or liver conditions should follow a clinician's specific guidance instead.

faq.question: Does this count water from food and other drinks?
faq.answer: No, this estimates total water-equivalent intake as a target; roughly a fifth of daily fluid typically comes from food, so plain drinking water needs may be somewhat lower in practice.

faq.question: Why does activity level matter?
faq.answer: More physical activity increases fluid loss through sweat, so the multiplier raises the daily target for moderate and active lifestyles.

faq.question: Is more water always better?
faq.answer: No. Drinking far beyond your body's needs can dilute blood sodium levels. This estimate is a reasonable target, not a floor to exceed aggressively.

name: Body Fat Percentage Calculator
shortDescription: Estimate body fat percentage using height, waist, neck and applicable hip measurements.
intro: Estimate body fat percentage using the U.S. Navy circumference method, which uses neck, waist, and, for women, hip measurements alongside height, rather than a scale that can't distinguish fat from muscle. Enter your measurements in centimeters, taken with a flexible tape at the points that method specifies, to see an estimated body fat percentage and a general category from essential fat through above average. This method is a widely used field estimate, not a laboratory-grade measurement like a DEXA scan.
how: For men: %BF = 495 ÷ (1.0324 − 0.19077 × log₁₀(waist − neck) + 0.15456 × log₁₀(height)) − 450. For women: %BF = 495 ÷ (1.29579 − 0.35004 × log₁₀(waist + hip − neck) + 0.22100 × log₁₀(height)) − 450. All measurements are in centimeters.

examples.input: Male: height 175 cm, waist 85 cm, neck 38 cm
Female: height 165 cm, waist 75 cm, hip 100 cm, neck 32 cm

limitations: Accuracy depends heavily on precise, consistent tape placement and is generally less accurate for very lean or very heavy individuals than lab methods like DEXA or hydrostatic weighing. This is an estimate for general awareness, not a medical or athletic-grade measurement.

faq.question: Where exactly do I measure my waist and neck?
faq.answer: Measure the neck just below the larynx, and the waist at the navel for men or at the narrowest point for women, keeping the tape snug but not compressing the skin.

faq.question: Why does the formula need a hip measurement for women only?
faq.answer: The U.S. Navy method uses separate validated formulas for each sex; the women's version was derived using hip circumference as an additional predictor, while the men's version was not.

faq.question: How does this compare to a DEXA scan?
faq.answer: DEXA scans directly measure fat, lean, and bone mass and are considered a gold standard. Tape-based estimates like this one are a convenient approximation, typically within a few percentage points for most body types.

name: Waist-to-Hip Ratio Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate waist-to-hip ratio from circumference measurements and view a general adult risk reference.
intro: Calculate waist-to-hip ratio from waist and hip circumferences measured in the same unit. Inspect the division and compare the result with the selected adult screening threshold. This reference describes population-level risk and cannot diagnose an individual or account for pregnancy, age, ethnicity or measurement error. Measure at consistent anatomical points, avoid pulling the tape tight, and repeat the measurements to check their consistency before interpreting the result.
how: Divide waist circumference by hip circumference. The WHO reference threshold for increased risk is 0.90 for men and 0.85 for women, including the boundary value. Below the threshold does not establish low individual risk.

examples.output: Ratio 0.90 · At or above the increased-risk threshold

limitations: This is a screening indicator, not a diagnosis. It does not account for muscle mass, frame size, ethnicity-specific thresholds, or other individual health factors. Measure both waist and hip at their widest natural points for consistent results.

faq.question: Where do I measure my hips?
faq.answer: Measure around the widest part of your hips and buttocks, keeping the tape level and snug but not compressing the skin.

faq.question: Why do men and women have different thresholds?
faq.answer: The reference thresholds are 0.90 for men and 0.85 for women. These are population screening references; individual assessment can require other measurements and clinical context.

faq.question: Is this the same as BMI?
faq.answer: No. BMI reflects overall weight relative to height, while waist-to-hip ratio reflects where fat is distributed, and the two provide different, complementary information.

name: Heart Rate Zone Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate five training heart rate zones in beats per minute from an age-predicted maximum heart rate.
intro: Find your estimated maximum heart rate and the five common training zones used in fitness plans, from an easy warm-up pace through your peak effort. Enter your age and see beats-per-minute ranges for warm up, fat burn, cardio, hard, and peak zones, which are useful for pacing workouts on a treadmill, bike, or heart-rate monitor. This uses the classic 220-minus-age formula, the version most fitness trackers and gym charts use, rather than a personally tested maximum from a supervised exercise test.
how: Estimated maximum heart rate is 220 minus your age in years. Each training zone is a percentage band of that maximum: Zone 1 (warm up) 50–60%, Zone 2 (fat burn) 60–70%, Zone 3 (cardio) 70–80%, Zone 4 (hard) 80–90%, and Zone 5 (peak) 90–100%.
limitations: The 220-minus-age formula is a population average with a fairly wide margin of error for any individual. Athletes, people on heart-rate-affecting medication, or anyone with a cardiac condition should get a personally tested maximum from a healthcare provider rather than relying on this estimate.

faq.question: Which zone should I train in to lose weight?
faq.answer: Zone 2, often called the fat-burn zone, uses a higher proportion of fat for fuel, but total calories burned across a longer, harder session can matter more for weight goals than the zone alone.

faq.question: Is 220 minus age the most accurate formula?
faq.answer: No single formula is exact for everyone. It's a widely used estimate; a supervised fitness test gives a more personally accurate maximum heart rate.

faq.question: Can medication affect these zones?
faq.answer: Yes. Some medications, such as beta blockers, lower your achievable heart rate, making these estimated zones inaccurate. Ask a healthcare provider for guidance if you take heart-rate-affecting medication.

name: Savings Goal Calculator
shortDescription: Calculate monthly savings needed to reach a target, with a balance growth chart and deposit schedule.
intro: Work out how much to set aside each month to reach a savings goal by a certain time, given what you've already saved and an assumed annual return. Enter your target amount, current savings, the number of months you have, and an expected annual return rate, and see the required monthly deposit. This mirrors the math behind the SIP calculator in reverse: instead of projecting where a monthly amount leads, it solves for the monthly amount a target requires.
how: With a monthly rate r derived from the annual rate, the required monthly deposit equals the shortfall between the goal and your current savings grown at that rate, divided by the future-value-of-annuity factor for the remaining months. At a 0% return, this simplifies to the shortfall divided evenly across the months. If existing savings and assumed growth already cover the target, the required deposit is zero.
limitations: Assumes a constant monthly return and deposits made at the end of each month, with no withdrawals. Real investments fluctuate, so treat the assumed return as an illustrative estimate rather than a guarantee.

faq.question: What if my current savings already exceed my goal?
faq.answer: The tool reports a required monthly deposit of zero and shows how far your current savings already exceed the target, before accounting for further growth.

faq.question: Should I use my bank's savings rate or an investment return?
faq.answer: Use whatever rate reasonably reflects where the money will actually sit. A savings account and an equity investment carry very different assumptions and risk.

faq.question: How is this different from the SIP calculator?
faq.answer: The SIP calculator projects the future value of a chosen monthly contribution. This tool works backward from a target future value to find the monthly contribution required.

name: Invoice Maker
shortDescription: Fill in a form and download a clean PDF invoice.
intro: Create a professional-looking invoice without a spreadsheet template or design software. Enter your business details, your client's details, an invoice number and dates, and as many line items as the job needs, and this tool lays them out on a clean single page with automatic subtotal, tax, and total calculations. Optionally add your company logo (PNG or JPEG, up to 2 MB) to appear at the top of the page. Add a currency symbol that matches your market and any notes your client should see, such as payment terms or bank details, then download a ready-to-send PDF. Everything is generated in your browser; no invoice data or logo is uploaded anywhere.
how: Each line item's quantity multiplied by its price is summed into a subtotal, tax is calculated as a percentage of that subtotal, and the total is their sum. Business and client details, an optional logo, the item table, and the totals are laid out directly onto an A4 PDF page using precise text positioning, with automatic wrapping for longer text and a new page added if the item list runs long.

examples.input: 3 line items, 8% tax, from Acme Studio to Globex Corp
examples.output: A one-page PDF: itemized table, subtotal, 8% tax, and total
The table continues automatically onto a second page

limitations: Supports one tax rate applied to the whole invoice, not per-item tax rates or multiple taxes. Only standard Latin-alphabet text renders; a handful of common symbols are substituted (for example, the rupee sign becomes "Rs.") and any other unsupported character is dropped rather than breaking the document. Maximum 30 line items.

faq.question: Can I reopen and edit an invoice later?
faq.answer: Not directly. This tool doesn't save your data between visits, so keep your entries in a note or spreadsheet if you'll need to recreate a similar invoice, or download and keep the PDF itself as your record.

faq.question: Does this send the invoice to my client?
faq.answer: No. It only generates a PDF file for you to download and send yourself, by email or any method you choose.

faq.question: Can I show multiple tax lines, like separate state and federal tax?
faq.answer: Not currently. Only a single combined tax rate is supported; calculate a combined rate first if your invoice needs to show more than one tax.

faq.question: Can I add my company logo?
faq.answer: Yes. Upload a PNG or JPEG up to 2 MB in the business details step, and it's placed at the top of the invoice, scaled to fit without stretching. It stays on your device like everything else in this tool.

name: Biodata Maker
shortDescription: Fill in a form and download a clean matrimonial biodata PDF.
